claims.text: Screen: all women of reproductive age, including pregnant and postpartum patients.
claims.quote: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for intimate partner violence (IPV) in women of reproductive age, including those who are pregnant and postpartum.

claims.text: Screen alone: ask when the patient is alone; the partner and anyone else with her can be asked to step away.
claims.quote: Ensuring privacy and confidentiality: Screen patients when they are alone. The partner and any other accompanying people can be asked to step away

claims.text: Safety: if she discloses abuse, assess safety and make a plan for now and later.
claims.quote: If the patient reports abuse, assess safety and make an appropriate plan to ensure immediate and subsequent safety.

claims.text: Document: record evidence of abuse, often with photographs; the record can support a legal case.
claims.quote: If intimate partner violence is confirmed, clinicians may be required to document the evidence of abuse, often by photographing the injuries. This documentation can be used to support a legal case against the perpetrator.

claims.text: Patient portal: the partner may be able to read the chart online.
claims.quote: Document carefully; consider that partners may have access to the patient's medical record through a patient online portal.

claims.text: Reporting: laws on reporting adult IPV vary by state and sometimes by type of clinician.
claims.quote: Laws about reporting intimate partner violence vary by state and sometimes by type of clinician (see MandatedReporter.com).
